cultural.vision_reason: The piece is labeled "ampang bilik," a Karo Batak house-altar term, and its carving style (pig figures, red/black/white pigment pattern) is characteristic of Batak art from Sumatra, not Toraja carving from Sulawesi, so this appears to be a different ethnic group's object mislabeled as Toraja.

physical.title: altar
physical.summary: House altar ("ampang bilik"); adzed from wood; two vertical beams of wood with two horizontal beams across (top one curved along bottom at ends); small cross-beam at each end between horizontal beams outside of vertical beams; rectangle of wood hanging down from top horizontal beam filling space between two vertical beams; smaller rectangle with curved top on top of top horizontal beam centred between two verticals; two three-dimensional pigs carved at centre along top of bottom horizontal beam; vertical beams carved with, from top to bottom: two human figures, sideways S shape, four interlocking S shapes, bird (possibly), two animals facing each other; top horizontal beam carved with birds at either end next to snakes with heads next to birds, tails almost meeting at centre; bottom horizontal beam carved with four interlocking S shapes at each end, then flower (possibly), human figure surrounded by animals at centre; centre rectangle carved with sets of three interlocking S shapes; carvings accented with red and white paint.
